scenario.title: Scoring Methodology Challenge — Construction Framework
scenario.description: BuildRight Ltd submitted a bid for a £2m construction framework. They were ranked second and excluded from the framework. They are challenging the scoring methodology, alleging that the quality scoring criteria were applied inconsistently and that the winning bidder received unjustifiably high marks in the 'social value' category despite providing less detailed evidence.

goals: Maintain transparency and fairness in evaluation process
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defending the procurement decision in the Technology and Construction Court (TCC) at a cost of £50k+ legal fees
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We acknowledge BuildRight Ltd's concerns regarding the scoring methodology, but we stand by our evaluation process which was conducted in accordance with the published evaluation criteria. We are willing to provide additional feedback and transparency to address their concerns.

interests: Winning the contract or securing a fair re-evaluation
Transparency — understanding exactly why you scored as you did
goals: Secure a re-evaluation of our bid with a focus on the quality scoring criteria and social value category
Obtain detailed, credible feedback to address concerns
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim or formal proceedings in the Technology and Construction Court (TCC) if no agreement is reached
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We request a re-evaluation of our bid with a specific focus on the quality scoring criteria and social value category, and we seek detailed feedback to address our concerns regarding inconsistent application of these criteria.

applicable_provisions: s12(1) Procurement Act 2023 - Value for Money
Regulation 84(2) Public Contracts Regulations 2015 - Evaluation Criteria
compliance_checks.reasoning: The Contracting Authority has provided a clear reference to the published evaluation criteria, which outlines the weightings and assessment methods for each category. The aggreived bidder's challenge focuses on an alleged inconsistency in scoring Quality Criterion Q4: 'Health and Safety Management'. However, at this stage, it is unclear whether the evaluation team applied the criteria inconsistently or if there was a genuine difference in interpretation.

applicable_provisions: s12(1) Procurement Act 2023: Value for Money
Regulation 84, Public Contracts Regulations 2015: Scoring and Evaluation
compliance_checks.reasoning: The Contracting Authority has acknowledged the Aggrieved Bidder's concerns and committed to an internal review of the scores awarded in Quality Criterion Q4. This demonstrates a willingness to investigate and potentially correct any errors. The Aggrieved Bidder has also provided specific details about their supporting evidence, which should aid in the evaluation team's inquiry.

Fusion21 has disclosed the evaluation team's scoring records for Quality Criterion Q4, as requested by BuildRight Ltd. The records will be disclosed in a redacted form to protect commercially sensitive information.

resolution_outcome: deadlock - max rounds reached, escalate to formal proceedings
